title: You weren’t lost.
paragraphs:
You weren’t lost.
You just didn’t want to be found.
And that’s the part we don’t say out loud.
Because hiding feels safer than being seen.

In the cool of the day, God walked into the garden…
and asked a question He already knew the answer to:
“Where are you?” (Genesis 3:9)
Not for His sake.
For Adam’s.

Because the moment sin entered, something deeper broke than behavior—
identity fractured.

Adam didn’t just eat the fruit.
He lost his place.
He said, “I heard You… and I was afraid… so I hid.” (Genesis 3:10)

Fear.
Shame.
Distance.
That’s the real exile.
And if we’re honest…
We’ve mastered hiding too.

Not behind trees—
but behind filtered lives, delayed obedience, quiet compromises.

We serve in ministry… but starve in secret.
We lift hands in worship… but bury conviction in silence.
We say, “I’m just tired.”
But deep down… we know we’re avoiding God.

Let me ask you something—
When was the last time God nudged you… and you delayed?
When was the last time you knew what was right… and chose comfort instead?

Not rebellion loud enough to scare you—
just quiet enough to justify.
That’s where hiding begins.

Some scholars interpret Genesis 3 not just as the fall of man…
but the birth of self-deception.

Because Adam didn’t run from God’s presence—
he ran from God’s voice.
And we do the same.

We scroll instead of praying.
We numb instead of confessing.
We explain instead of repenting.
Read that again.
Here’s the AHA moment:

God’s question was never about geography.
It was about honesty.

“Where are you?”
means
“Will you admit where sin has taken you?”
And here’s the mirror:

You’re not as hidden as you think—
you’re just not as surrendered as you know.
But here’s where grace explodes into the story.
Because God didn’t wait for Adam to come back.
He went after him.

The first voice after sin…
was not judgment.
It was pursuit.
And that same pursuit didn’t stop in Eden.
It carried all the way to a cross.

Because another Man would stand exposed—
not hiding behind leaves,
but hanging in your place.
Jesus Christ didn’t ask, “Where are you?”
He declared, “It is finished.” (John 19:30)

Where Adam covered himself,
Jesus uncovered Himself.

Where Adam hid in shame,
Jesus bore it in public.

Where Adam ran from God,
Jesus was forsaken so you could come near.
Let this confront you:

You can’t call it “struggle” forever
if you’re not willing to call it sin.
But don’t miss this…
Romans 5:8 says that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

Not when you fixed yourself.
Not when you cleaned up.
While you were still hiding.

That means your worst moment…
is not your disqualification.
It’s the very place grace wants to meet you.
You are not the version of you that failed last night.
You are the one God is calling out of hiding today.
So… where are you?

Still covering?
Still delaying?
Still negotiating with conviction?
Or ready to step into the light?
This is your moment.
Not to pretend.
Not to perform.
But to respond.

Repent.
Return.
Receive.
Because 1 John 1:9 promises—if we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us and cleanse us.
Cleanse.
Not shame you.

If your heart is burning right now…
that’s not guilt crushing you.
That’s God calling you.

And if you’re hungry for more—
not just posts, but deeper transformation—
Not information.
Formation.
And the next message might be the one that finally breaks what you’ve been hiding.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
